editorial:
Malice in the Palace is a Columbia Pictures Three Stooges short directed by Jules White and released September 1, 1949. It was the 117th Stooges entry, with Moe, Larry and Shemp Howard and Vernon Dent. The Stooges run a desert restaurant and go after an Emir's stolen diamond dressed as Santa Clauses. It was remade in 1956 as Rumpus in the Harem using stock footage from this film. It appears on budget home-video compilations and in several Internet Archive uploads, which makes it an easy pick for a reuser.

The rights trap is the renewal. Wikipedia says this short is public domain, but it gives 1964 as the expiry year. A 1949 release would have needed renewal in 1977, so that date looks wrong and I treat the claim as unconfirmed. Until someone checks the 1977 Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes and the Copyright Office records, the print is undetermined. A free Internet Archive upload does not prove a clear copyright status. The colorized upload may carry added material.
faq: Is Malice in the Palace public domain in the US?

Not confirmed. It was released in 1949, so a renewal would have been due in 1977. I could not open the renewal records. Wikipedia calls it public domain, but its stated 1964 expiry does not fit a 1949 release. Search the Stanford renewal database and the 1977 Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes yourself before relying on it.
Can I use the Internet Archive copies or the colorized version?

The Internet Archive hosting a copy does not settle the rights. The colorized upload adds material that may carry its own claim. Check the print's renewal status first, and avoid reusing the colorization unless you know who made it.
